headline: Bill would have required colleges getting federal student aid to tell students about rights and resources for carrying a pregnancy to term.
what_it_does: Colleges and universities that take part in federal student aid programs would have had to give certain information to prospective and current students. This would have included a list of on-campus and community resources to help pregnant students carry a baby to term and care for the baby after birth. Schools would also have had to explain available accommodations for pregnant and parenting students and how to file a discrimination complaint related to a student's decision to carry a baby to term. The Senate did not advance the bill on January 27, 2026.

who_it_affects.group: Colleges and universities that participate in federal student aid programs
who_it_affects.how: They would have been required to collect and share information on resources, accommodations, and complaint procedures for pregnant students.

who_it_affects.group: Pregnant college students and students who may become pregnant
who_it_affects.how: They would have received information about support resources, accommodations for pregnancy and parenting, and how to file discrimination complaints.
They would have received this information from schools before enrolling.
